parts.label: a
parts.technique: impulse-momentum for collision
parts.reason: Impulse and momentum in collisions is not mentioned in any M-statement listed (only kinematics, forces/Newton's laws, moments are covered); no statement covers conservation of momentum or impulse.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: conservation of linear momentum
parts.reason: Requires conservation of momentum, which no statement covers; also depends on impulse concept from (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles (towing)
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly includes connected particle problems, and resolving forces along direction of motion for whole system uses M8.2/M8.4.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: tension in tow-bar via Newton's second law on one particle
parts.reason: Same connected particles context as (a), covered by M8.4 guidance.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: equilibrium of forces given as vectors
parts.reason: M8.4/M8.5 cover equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces and resolving/addition of vectors given in i-j form.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: magnitude of resultant vector
parts.reason: Finding magnitude of a resultant force vector is covered by M8.5 and general vector magnitude P10.2.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: angle of vector relative to unit vector j
parts.reason: Finding direction of a vector using trigonometry (tan) is within ordinary vector work (P10.2) and forces (M8.5), not requiring dot product since simple right-triangle trig used in mark scheme.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: moments - taking moments about a point, tipping condition
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers moments in simple static contexts including problems on the point of tipping.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: moments - finding reaction force
parts.reason: Continuation of moments problem, covered by M9.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat under gravity (vertical motion)
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion, and M8.3 covers motion under gravity with g constant.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat for greatest height
parts.reason: Standard constant acceleration formula application, covered by M7.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: suvat with quadratic equation for time interval above a height
parts.reason: Uses s=ut+1/2at^2 solved via quadratic, both covered by M7.3 (constant acceleration formulae) and P2.3 (quadratic solving).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat for deceleration time
parts.reason: Constant acceleration formula, M7.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: sketching speed-time graph
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers interpreting/using graphs in kinematics including speed-time graphs.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: area under speed-time graph = distance, solve for unknown time
parts.reason: M7.2 covers area under velocity-time graph representing distance; combined with algebra to solve for T.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: finding acceleration from gradient/suvat
parts.reason: M7.2/M7.3 cover gradient interpretation and constant acceleration formulae.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: sketching acceleration-time graph
parts.reason: M7.2 covers graphs in kinematics; sketching acceleration-time graph is a natural extension consistent with gradient interpretation content, though not explicitly named 'acceleration-time graph'.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: speed from velocity vector (magnitude)
parts.reason: P10.2 covers calculating magnitude of a vector; M7.3 covers vectors in kinematics.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: position vector as function of time
parts.reason: M7.3 explicitly covers suvat in 2D using vectors, e.g. r = r0 + vt form.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: equating vector components to find time when one point is due west of another
parts.reason: Uses vector components and position vectors, covered by M7.3/P10 vector work (equating j-components), standard geometric vector problem.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: distance between two position vectors
parts.reason: P10.4 covers calculating distance between points from position vectors.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: resolving forces on inclined plane, Newton's second law with zero acceleration (constant speed)
parts.reason: M8.2 guidance covers resolving forces on inclined plane; M8.3 covers weight component; constant speed means equilibrium perpendicular to plane.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: friction model F=μR on inclined plane with constant velocity
parts.reason: M8.6 explicitly covers F≤μR model, coefficient of friction, motion on rough surface, combined with M8.2 inclined plane resolution.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law with friction and gravity component to find deceleration then suvat for distance
parts.reason: Combines M8.2 (inclined plane), M8.6 (friction), M8.3 (gravity), M7.3 (suvat) - all covered.
